answer: An agent economy can use bond-backed quadratic voting: each identity locks a slashable bond, and voting weight rises only with the square root of it. The pool is an ocean that no key-splitting can enlarge; sqrt weighting makes each shard count less, so a Sybil attacker pays the same capital for a smaller voice. A shared atlas maps bonds to auditable reputations, and a sudden delta in fresh accounts flags one source funding them. Faking identities thus costs locked collateral plus slashing risk, far pricier than honest play.
